items.item_text: 01. Please indicate how you meet minimum educational requirements for this position. Provide a legible copy of your college/university transcript(s) in your online application packet. Copies of diplomas are not acceptable in lieu of college transcripts. Short-term workshops will not be accepted as fulfilling any part of the education requirement.

02. Please describe your increasing responsible experience providing technical user support services and/or maintaining, supporting and repairing computers, software applications, audio/visual equipment and telecommunications equipment. Include employer names(s), position title(s), dates of employment, full-time or part-time status (hours per week), your roles, and responsibilities. Please provide your total years of full-time experience in this field.
03. Please describe your experience training or assisting employees or students with technology.
04. Please describe your customer service experience and the roles you have played in serving the public.
05. Please describe your experience coordinating a project, assignment, or workload involving multiple people or departments.
06. Please describe your experience supporting both Windows/PC and Apple/Mac computers.
07. Please describe your ability to work successfully in a multicultural, diverse environment.
08. Why do you want to work at College of the Canyons in this Lead Information Technology Coordinator position?

Provides leadership within the department and coordinates projects and other assignments requiring a high level of responsibility and independence. Provides expertise and support for major IT projects and systems impacting multiple departments.
Performs duties to ensure proper operation and security of the computer systems, network equipment and servers to provide technology resources for District faculty, staff and students.

Performs advanced project management tasks such as plan, manage, organize, and schedule project timelines, resource allocation, oversee and document all aspects of large scale projects that impacts both CCC and VLC.
Participates in the planning, administration and maintenance of technical functions and matters related to multi-vendor equipment and software.
Installs and maintains a variety of equipment including computers, laptops, printers, scanners and other peripherals.
Performs user help desk functions and operations; use a record-keeping system to log requests and track resolution of problems.

Plans and coordinates various workshops and training sessions related to the use of District computer and audio/visual technology to employees over the phone, at their work location and in one-on-one, small group and classroom training environments.
Assists and coordinates the checkout of equipment to District faculty and staff.

Recommends the purchase of new and replacement equipment. Requisitions, orders and stores spare and replacement parts. Schedules repairs and completes related paperwork for warranty claims as necessary.
Performs scheduled maintenance and repairs of computer and audio/visual equipment; troubleshoots and repairs computers, peripherals, audio/visual equipment and software applications.
Installs, configures, updates and maintains a variety of computer and audio/visual equipment including projectors, computers, printers, scanners, televisions and other peripherals.

Operates testing and measurement devices, computer diagnostic software and other specialized instruments used in the repair and maintenance of computer equipment, audio/visual equipment and related peripherals.
Consults with various departments to determine current and future technical needs; works with faculty and staff on acquiring equipment for evaluations and purchase.

Provides assistance to students, faculty and staff on utilizing computer and software programs including remote access and the proper use of audio-visual equipment in conjunction with computers and peripherals.
Assists in the maintenance of user accounts on the system.

Works in a team environment with other members of the Information Technology staff to maintain the district's network infrastructure and support users in departments and offices throughout the district.
Maintains a current and accurate inventory of computer hardware, software, audio/visual equipment and licenses owned or leased by the district.
Prepares instructions on the installation and use of district supported hardware and application programs.
Connects computers and peripherals to the campus network (both wired and wireless) including cabling when necessary, network protocol configuration and NIC installation.
Tests software performance prior to releasing new applications for desktop and network use.
Maintains end-user Operating Systems and application programs on PC and Macintosh desktop environments to ensure proper operation.
Provides direction to part-time employees and assists in the training of employees in the lower technician classifications.
Drives to various locations to setup and modify new and existing audio visual equipment.
Attends meetings as assigned.
Performs other duties as assigned.
A wide variety of equipment used in audio visual support services.
Computerized and electronic equipment including computers, peripherals, audio/visual units and other related office equipment.
Principles of training and basic instruction reinforcement techniques for providing direction in the use of computers, software and Audio Visual equipment.
Both PC and Macintosh desktop environments and operating systems.

Working knowledge of commercial software packages and operating systems including but not limited to the Microsoft Windows current and previous operating systems, Microsoft Office, Internet Explorer, Microsoft Outlook, Photoshop, Acrobat reader and Mac OS.
Computer hardware peripherals including but not limited to scanners, digital cameras, and printers.
Computer networking equipment, testing devices and cabling standards.
Information systems technology and terms including recent developments in networking and computer technology.
Methods and procedures used in the maintenance and repair of electronics systems and instruments.
Oral and written communication skills.
Plan, schedule and perform simple and complex user support activities in an organized manner.
Use computers and computer technology in daily duties.
Use initiative and problem-solving skills in carrying out responsibilities.
Perform skilled technical work in the installation, maintenance and repair of computers, software, audio/visual and telecommunications equipment.
Lead and coordinate the work of others.
Maintain current knowledge of technical advances in all areas of responsibility.
Read and interpret technical manuals.
Keep detailed, precise records and handle correspondence effectively.
Evaluate and recommend equipment and installations based on new technologies.
Work and communicate effectively and cooperatively with students, Information Technology staff and other District staff.
Work independently while meeting schedules and timelines.
Work varied hours including evenings and weekends as necessary.
Demonstrate interpersonal skills using tact, patience and courtesy.
Demonstrate sensitivity to and understanding of the diverse academic, socio-economic, cultural, disability and ethnic backgrounds of staff and students.
